_comment: Single source of the Lab Member row-level visibility rules (ADR-0011, docs/adr/0011-row-level-visibility.md; A1 record access,
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-record-access-design.md).
scripts/gen_access_rules.py turns this file into the Lab Member directus_permissions rows. Its output is pasted into
scripts/configure_users_and_policies.sql (gen_access_rules.py --write) and into the migration that applies it;
tests/phase1_schema.sh and tests/scripts/test_access_rules.py fail when either drifts from this file.
READ visibility is not written here: who can read a record is decided in SQL (d1_private.readers_of_*, migration 166) and stored in
the <type>_readers tables, kept by triggers. A read rule is therefore one of: {"readers": "some"} (a record type: the top-level
`readers` alias, `readers: {_some: {user_id: $CURRENT_USER}}`; with "open_to_all": true for the orphan amnesty, an OR with the
`open_to_all` alias), or, for a child of a record, a set that reaches the parent's readers through one bare hop (`reader.*` below).
UPDATE, DELETE and MANAGE stay Directus filters (a record's manage rule is its delete rule): the reader term AND the editor/owner test.
A rule is a SET: a list (OR) or {"and": [...]} (AND). An item is a user-leaf path that ends at a user column that must equal the signed-in user
($CURRENT_USER); {"set": ..., "via": "sample_id"} (another set with every path prefixed by a relation field, which must be to-one; no via = as is);
{"reader": "bare"} (the bare hop `readers.user_id = $CURRENT_USER` at the row's prefix: the caller is a reader of the record; used with via
for children and in update/delete rules, never as a `_some`); {"path", "at", "where"} (a user leaf plus `role _in [...]` on the same row
of the junction `at`); {"field", "eq" | "null"} (a literal leaf); {"unless_restricted": [...]} (restricted = false AND the items, on the row the
prefix points at); and nested {"and": [...]} / {"or": [...]}. See the docstring of scripts/gen_access_rules.py.
Directus 11.17 accepts `_some` only directly under a top-level O2M: the generator drops the others (a bare to-many hop means "any joined row").
A legal `_some` also applies the related collection's rule FOR THE SAME ACTION to the rows it looks at, so the readers tables' own read rule is
trivial (own rows) and an update or delete rule must not use one (sample_co_owners update is owner-only: `co_owners._some` in sample.editors
would stop every co-owner from editing); update and delete read the bare hop `readers.user_id`, which applies no rule.
Directus reads a relation key by its first key only and fails a `_some` whose body is not one plain chain, so a role test is an AND of two bare paths.
'rules' lists, per collection and action, the set that filters it (or the read kind above), or "any" for no filter. Directus does not apply item
filters to create, so create is always "any". 'unfiltered' is every other Lab Member grant: reference data and the rows
added by later migrations. A new collection that holds lab data needs an entry in 'rules', not in 'unfiltered'.
The eleven *_params tables in 'unfiltered' no longer exist (migration 20260623000032 folded them into columns of manufacturing_operations and
test_sessions, so they follow those rows' rules); their stale rows stay here only so the drift checks see every row in directus_permissions.
'custom' holds the rows that need more than a filter: per collection and action, any of permissions, validation and
fields (a list; written as the comma-separated text Directus stores). 'guards' lists the junctions whose rows grant
visibility: Directus does not filter create, so the d1-access-guard hook (core/extensions/d1-access-guard) refuses
to create or repoint one unless the caller passes the parent's rule named by 'rule' (default update). A junction also counts when a column a
read path uses is derived from it: test_sessions.sample_id is kept equal to the first sample of test_sessions_subject
(migration 139), so adding a subject row to a test can change who reads that test. gen_access_rules.py writes that rule
into core/extensions/d1-access-guard/rules.json. 'field' is the junction's FK to the parent, 'key' the parent's primary key.
'owner_guards' lists the records whose update rule is wider than their delete rule (co-owners and Can edit people may update, only the
owner may delete). Changing one of their 'fields' (the owner column, restricted) would hand delete or visibility rights to the editor, so the
same hook refuses an update that changes one unless the caller passes the record's delete rule (they are its current owner). 'key' is the
record's primary key, a field's 'value_key' the primary key of the table the field points to. gen_access_rules.py fails when a ruled
collection has different update and delete filters and no entry here.
'restricted_keys' lists, per record type, the keys that move a record between parents (and so change who sees it): when the record or an old
or new parent is restricted, the hook asks for the record's delete rule. 'record_access' tells d1-record-access (the endpoint that is the only
writer of the five *_access tables) where each record type keeps its access list.
